newsitem.title: USA: Perry says Gulf coalition "alive and well".
newsitem.headline: Perry says Gulf coalition "alive and well".

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday that he found the Western-Arab Gulf coalition "alive and well" during weekend visits to key allies and that all support recent U.S. actions against Iraq.

The bottom line ... is that the coalition is alive and well," Perry said at a press briefing of his visits to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Turkey and Britain, where he met with French and British defense ministers. "They offered complete agreement on the (U.S.) containment policy (of Iraq), which I described to them." He said that all the allies he had visited supported the U.S. decision to expand the no-fly zone over southern Iraq except for France.

Perry at first said the coalition leaders he had conferred with in the Gulf and in Britain "offered support to Operation Southern Watch and said they will continue to support Operation Southern Watch in its expanded form."

Southern Watch is the code name for U.S., British and French air patrols designed to exclude Iraqi aircraft from a zone covering southern Iraq. Perry said allied support covered both a U.S. decision to expand that zone northward from the 32rd to the 33nd parallel and to increase the number of patrols.
Later, however, he said France did not support the geographic expansion of the zone.

Clinton sent Perry on a whirlwind tour of key Gulf capitals as well as Ankara and London over the weekend amid widespread reports that the coalition was being torn apart by dissension over recent U.S. military strikes against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's forces.
